findings.title: Restore read-only sandbox for codex exec
findings.whyItBreaks: The diff deletes `-s read-only` from the codex invocation. `-s`/`--sandbox` is the ONLY thing constraining codex to read-only (possible values: read-only, workspace-write, danger-full-access). Without it, codex falls back to its default sandbox mode (`workspace-write`), so the `spawnSync(bin, args, { cwd: opts.repoPath, input: prompt })` call now lets the model-generated shell commands create/modify/delete files and run tooling inside `opts.repoPath` instead of being limited to reads. This is a security regression in a harness that runs an AI agent against a target repo; a prompt or model misstep can now mutate/corrupt the repository rather than merely read it.

findings.title: Removing -s read-only drops enforced read-only sandbox on codex agent
findings.whyItBreaks: `runCodex` spawns `codex exec` with `cwd: opts.repoPath` (line 24), so the sandbox policy governs the target repo it operates on. The diff deletes the explicit `-s read-only` arg, which previously FIXED the sandbox to read-only for every call. After the change the sandbox mode is whatever codex defaults to or reads from the caller's `~/.codex/config.toml` (or an injected `-c sandbox_mode=...`). Codex's `-s/--sandbox` accepts `read-only`, `workspace-write`, `danger-full-access` (verified via `codex exec --help`); any writable ambient config now lets the spawned agent write to / run commands in the repo it was asked to inspect. `runCodex` is exported and its prior contract was 'run codex read-only'; that guarantee is gone and callers can no longer rely on non-mutation. If writable behavior was intended it should be explicit and opt-in, not inherited from an unrelated global config. Note: codex's default sandbox is read-only, so under a pristine config this is behaviorally a no-op; the regression materializes when a caller's config permits writes.

findings.title: Restore read-only sandbox for codex subprocess
findings.whyItBreaks: `runCodex` spawns `codex exec` against `opts.repoPath` and feeds it a prompt; `-s`/`--sandbox` selects the sandbox policy used when executing *model-generated shell commands* (possible values `read-only`, `workspace-write`, `danger-full-access` — verified via `codex exec --help`). The removed `-s read-only` forced those commands to be read-only. Without it, the sandbox mode falls back to the codex config's `sandbox_mode`, which is environment-dependent and overridable to a write-permissive value (in this box `~/.codex/config.toml` sets `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` and the `codex` shim adds `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`). A codex agent analyzing a repo can now modify the repo/files instead of being constrained to read, and the write path does not depend on the `--output-last-message` write (that file lives in `os.tmpdir()`, outside the sandboxed workspace), so removing the flag is not needed for output. The helper is exported and is the only codex invocation path, so every caller loses the read-only guarantee.
